name: Question 15
problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under a **clockwise** rotation of ${135}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(0,0)$
- $(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})$
- $(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})$
worked_solution:
The rotation matrix ${R}_{\theta }$ represents a rotation of angle $\theta $ counterclockwise about the origin and is given by

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}],
$$

Substituting $\theta =-{135}^{∘}$ into the above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-{135}^{∘}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{135}^{∘}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(-{135}^{∘}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(-{135}^{∘})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the transformation, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the rotation $R$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the coordinates of ${S}^{′}$ are

$$
(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}),\,(0,0),\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}).
$$

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."

Question 15

A triangle S has vertices at (1,0),(0,0),(0,1). Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of S′, the image of S under a clockwise rotation of 135∘ about the origin?

  1. (0,0)
  2. (12,−12)
  3. (−12,12)
a
I only
b
I and III only
c
II only
d
I and II only
e
II and III only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The rotation matrix Rθ represents a rotation of angle θ counterclockwise about the origin and is given by

R=[cos⁡θ−sin⁡θsin⁡θcos⁡θ],

Substituting θ=−135∘ into the above, we have

R=[cos⁡(−135∘)−sin⁡(−135∘)sin⁡(−135∘)cos⁡(−135∘)]=[−1212−12−12]=12[−11−1−1].

To find the image of S under the transformation, we first create a matrix X containing all of the vertices of S:

X=[100001]

Now, we compute the image of X under the rotation R by calculating the matrix product RX:

RX=12[−11−1−1][100001]=12[−101−10−1]=[−12012−120−12]

Therefore the coordinates of S′ are (−12,−12),(0,0),(12,−12).

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."
